method: Source, archive facts, parsed call/flow facts, full scripts and HTML loading paths, plus isolated API-mocked replay. No network requests or appliance exploitation performed.
placement_review: Port observation is service-neutral; no required ComfyUI content. Socket port wins over service identity.
DOM listener observes UI interaction; HTTP transmission is not required. Form-input wins over HTTP form transport.
Input-object spread and JSON POST body binding belongs in HTTP request payload; neither serialization alone nor telemetry naming establishes exfiltration.
scope_changes: Port atom retains Python/shell, Windows/Unix and Calvyn exclusion; adds a numeric boundary to reject port 81880.
DOM listener matcher and effective scope preserved; all five exact consumer locations updated. No source/destination ancestor-directory selectors found.
Numeric endpoint POST now requires the incoming function object to be spread into the object actually serialized; replaces the redundant generic POST-body leg.
Wallet hostile composite retains arbitrary reporting-callback names and the external-IP JSON beacon sink; numeric POST branch is strengthened by input-to-body binding.
consumer_audit: New payload atom is a stricter subset of existing fetch JSON request capabilities. Broad HTTP request consumers retain protocol semantics; no additional source/intent role is supplied. Existing hostile counts remain unchanged.
controls: Six positive/near-miss fixtures passed: renamed input/payload/URL builder, unrelated JSON object, local-only submit handler, SMA service port, port-prefix near miss, and genuine ComfyUI name/endpoint.
limitations: Static relationships support attempts and capabilities; mocked replay verifies generated requests, not server receipt or exploit success.
regression: First full validation caught loss of renamed sendData beacon variant; removed callback-name restriction and retained original beacon coverage.
